title: Upanishad's Perspective on Life and Truth
content: No one has ever won in this world. Everyone thinks they have lost. To others, they seem to be living a normal life. For some, they have made it. If we look closely, no one has won here. Everyone thinks they have lost. The Upanishad begins by praying to the sun and states that air is 'pratyksha bramha,' or visible truth. Despite being invisible, air is a symbol for truth because it is always present, touching our bodies and eyes, yet we cannot see it. This reflects the idea that truth is everywhere, like air, and we are all dependent on it to live.
raw_text:
Noone has ever won in this world. Everyone thing of themselves as they are defeated. They think they have lost it. But to others he is living a normal life. For some he has made it. If we look closely noone has won here. Everyone thinks they have lost.

Upanishad starts with praying to sun. And specially it says that air is "pratyksha bramha" (visible truth). But air is invisible then why? Cause truth is like air. It's there everywhere. We are all dependent on air to live. It always touch our body and aur eye. Still we can't see it. So it's a symbol for truth.
